buyer_specs: Typical full-apartment budget: €40,000–150,000 (about 60–100 m² at roughly €600–1,500 per m²)
Contract, quote and progress reports in English
Alvará (IMPIC construction licence) in a class that covers the contract value
Written scope with milestone payments, not a large upfront deposit
Someone named on site daily, with photo or WhatsApp updates for owners abroad
Clear answer on who files permits and who deals with the condominium and Câmara

faq.a: Contractors taking on work above minor repairs are expected to hold an IMPIC alvará in a class that covers the contract value. Ask for the number and look it up on the IMPIC public register yourself.
faq.q: Do I need a contractor with an alvará?

faq.a: Commonly around three to six months for a full flat once permits are settled, and longer with structural work or heritage-building constraints. Ask for a dated schedule tied to payment milestones.
faq.q: How long does a full apartment renovation take?

faq.a: Yes, if you set it up properly: an English-language contract, a named site lead, weekly photo updates, milestone payments and a Portuguese NIF. Avoid paying large sums before work is visible.
faq.q: Can I manage the renovation from abroad?

faq.a: A reduced 6% VAT rate can apply to some rehabilitation and renovation works, depending on the property and the type of work. Confirm eligibility with your accountant and ask the contractor how they will invoice.

glossary.Alvará: Construction licence issued by IMPIC to a contracting company, graded by class and category of work.
glossary.Certidão de não dívida: Certificate that a company has no tax or social-security debt.
glossary.Condomínio: The owners' association; its rules and approval can affect noise hours, façade and shared-structure changes.
glossary.Câmara Municipal: The city council (Lisbon's is the Câmara Municipal de Lisboa) that handles building permits and notifications.
glossary.IMPIC: Instituto dos Mercados Públicos, do Imobiliário e da Construção, the national body that licenses contractors and keeps the public register.
glossary.Licenciamento / comunicação prévia: The permit route (licence) and the lighter prior-notification route for works that need council control.
glossary.Livro de Reclamações: The official complaints book that Portuguese businesses must offer; available online at livroreclamacoes.pt.
glossary.NIF: Portuguese tax number, needed to sign contracts and receive invoices.
glossary.Pombalino / gaioleiro: Two older Lisbon building types (post-1755 timber-braced and late-19th-century), where opening walls needs structural checks.
